metadata.title: Stochastic Backpropagation and Approximate Inference in Deep Generative Models (Rezende, Mohamed, Wierstra, 2014)
metadata.framework: stochastic backpropagation through Gaussian latent variables for deep generative model inference
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1401.4082.

nodes.name: Deep latent Gaussian model (DLGM)
nodes.statement: A hierarchical generative model with $L$ layers of Gaussian latent variables: $\mathbf{z}_L \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$, $\mathbf{z}_l | \mathbf{z}_{l+1} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_l(\mathbf{z}_{l+1}), \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}_l^2(\mathbf{z}_{l+1})))$ for $l = L-1, \ldots, 1$, and $\mathbf{x} | \mathbf{z}_1 \sim p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z}_1)$. The means and variances are computed by neural networks with parameters $\theta$. This defines a deep, directed generative model.

nodes.name: Variational free energy (ELBO)
nodes.statement: The variational free energy (ELBO): $\mathcal{F}(\theta, \phi) = \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})} [\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}) - \log q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})] = \mathbb{E}_{q_\phi}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}|\mathbf{z})] - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) \| p_\theta(\mathbf{z})) \le \log p_\theta(\mathbf{x})$. Maximizing $\mathcal{F}$ jointly optimizes the generative model and recognition model.

nodes.name: Recognition model (approximate posterior)
nodes.statement: The recognition model $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x})$ is a Gaussian with mean and variance produced by a neural network (the recognition/inference network): $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}_l|\mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_\phi^l(\mathbf{x}), \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}_\phi^{2,l}(\mathbf{x})))$. For the hierarchical case, $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{l=1}^L q_\phi(\mathbf{z}_l | \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}_{<l})$.

nodes.name: Gaussian backpropagation (reparameterization / stochastic backprop)
nodes.statement:
For a Gaussian $q_\phi(\mathbf{z}|\mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{N}( oldsymbol{\mu}, C)$ with mean $ oldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance $C$ depending on $\phi$: write $\mathbf{z} =  oldsymbol{\mu} + R  oldsymbol{\epsilon}$ where $C = RR^	op$ and $ oldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$. Then $
abla_\phi \mathbb{E}_q[f(\mathbf{z})] = \mathbb{E}_{ oldsymbol{\epsilon}} [
abla_\phi f( oldsymbol{\mu} + R  oldsymbol{\epsilon})]$ which can be estimated by sampling $ oldsymbol{\epsilon}$. This is the 'Gaussian backpropagation' rule. For general distributions, an additional correction term involving $
abla_{\mathbf{z}} \log q$ (Bonnet's and Price's theorems) arises.

nodes.name: Structured variational inference with normalizing flows (mention)
nodes.statement: The paper mentions that the Gaussian recognition model can be made more flexible by applying a sequence of invertible smooth mappings (normalizing flows) to the initial Gaussian sample, yielding a richer variational family while maintaining tractable density evaluation via the change-of-variables formula.

nodes.name: Bonnet's theorem (Gaussian integration by parts)
nodes.statement: For $\mathbf{z} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, C)$ and differentiable $f$: $\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\mu}} \mathbb{E}[f(\mathbf{z})] = \mathbb{E}[\nabla_{\mathbf{z}} f(\mathbf{z})]$ (Bonnet's theorem). This is a special case of Stein's identity.
conclusions: Gradient w.r.t. mean equals expected gradient w.r.t. sample

nodes.name: Price's theorem (covariance derivative)
nodes.statement:
For $\mathbf{z} \sim \mathcal{N}( oldsymbol{\mu}, C)$: $
abla_{C_{ij}} \mathbb{E}[f(\mathbf{z})] =  rac{1}{2} \mathbb{E}[
abla_{z_i} 
abla_{z_j} f(\mathbf{z})]$ (Price's theorem). This provides the gradient of the expectation w.r.t. covariance entries.
conclusions: Gradient w.r.t. covariance equals half the expected Hessian of $f$

nodes.name: Unbiased gradient estimator for DLGM training
nodes.statement: Using Gaussian backpropagation, the gradient of $\mathcal{F}$ w.r.t. both $\theta$ and $\phi$ can be estimated with low variance: $\nabla_{\theta,\phi} \mathcal{F} = \mathbb{E}_{\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I)} [\nabla_{\theta,\phi} (\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}, g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})) - \log q_\phi(g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon})|\mathbf{x}))]$ where $g_\phi(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}) = \boldsymbol{\mu}_\phi + R_\phi \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$. This enables end-to-end training of DLGMs via standard backpropagation.
conclusions: Unbiased, low-variance gradient estimator for both generative and recognition parameters
End-to-end training via standard backpropagation + sampling

nodes.name: MNIST generative modeling
nodes.statement: DLGM with 1 and 2 layers of stochastic latent variables trained on MNIST. With 2 layers, achieves marginal likelihood bound comparable to the VAE. Demonstrates smooth latent-space interpolation and meaningful learned representations.
